What makes bitcoin the dominant cryptocurrency compared to the competitors?
hmm, is the first one and is the one that has a better logo ;)

I think it is simply because so many people have so much of it. I see some definite problems with it compared to newer crypto-currencies such as the fact that mining has become an arms race where pure processing power is rewarded as opposed to contributions to the ledgers.

That's really interesting, thanks for the insight! It did seem a bit complicated with the whole giant mining groups trying to outdo each other. Do you think Bitcoin will remain, or will these newer ones usurp it?

Problem with the giant mining groups is the forking problem that occurs if one of the groups ever becomes greater than 50% of the network. And this has come close to happening several times. Once this happens, that group controls the ledger and can theoretically create false transactions. This is an admitted flaw that appears in original white paper. It was just never imagined that single groups could get this large. Since there are now mining pools, however, groups can get this large. I think it was an unforeseen eventuality that could potentially cause problems for bitcoin.

I think that cryptocurrency will succeed in coming years, but bitcoin has two or three problems like this one, that may hold it back.

such as the fact that mining has become an arms race where pure processing power is rewarded as opposed to contributions to the ledgers

I don't know a lot about other cryptocurrencies, could you put an example about that? I mean, what mechanisms are used to avoid that "arms race" in other coins?

Primarily the 'network effect' - you'll want to use the same money everyone else uses. There's far more liquidity in bitcoin than all the rest put together.

Second, few competitors offer any features that significantly improve on bitcoin's value as a currency. Some offer novel, possibly better, network security mechanisms ('scrypt' coins, primecoin) but the Bitcoin network's sheer size makes it by far the most secure. None of these novel alternatives actually offer much of an improved buying/saving/spending experience. Some do have unique smart-contract features (NXT), but apparently nothing exciting enough to knock Bitcoin off it's throne - besides there are tools in development to add all those features to Bitcoin - taking advantage of it's massive network security without having to build out a bunch of mining power for a new 'coin.'
